title: Patriarchate of Aquileia
capsule: The Patriarchate of Aquileia was both an ecclesiastical province and a temporal feudal principality in northeastern Italy, whose patriarchs traced their authority to apostolic-era evangelization of the region and whose title emerged formally during the sixth-century Three Chapters Schism. At its medieval apex, patriarchal jurisdiction encompassed northeastern Italy, Istria, Carniola, Carinthia, and Rhaetia, and temporal rule was recognized in a 1077 grant; Venetian expansion and Habsburg pressure progressively eroded this authority from the fourteenth century onward. Pope Benedict XIV suppressed the patriarchate by the 1751 bull Injunctio Nobis, dividing its territory between the new archdioceses of Udine and Gorizia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Institutional history is well documented in papal and Venetian records; the outer limits of temporal control varied considerably across the centuries and are reconstructed with moderate confidence from feudal surveys and chronicles.
